Thermal protection of gas turbine blades, combustors, and some rocket nozzles is generally provided by thin superficial layer coatings of yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ).
YSZ has exceptionally low thermal conductivity up to high temperatures, but its resistance to radiative heat transport was not well understood.
The researchers developed a continuum model for combined radiative and conductive heat transport through a coating, implemented in MATLAB.
Crucial to minimizing radiative heating through a coating is a highly reflecting layer placed in the coating, but preliminary attempts using platinum or gold proved microstructurally unstable.
The researchers demonstrated that the optical scattering coefficient can be obtained from measurements of the diffuse optical reflectance.
There appears to be a direct correlation between the spectral optical diffuse reflectance and the thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity of the coatings examined.
Infiltration of an EB-PVD coating with an epoxy having a similar refractive index to CMAS significantly decreased the optical scattering coefficient.
The researchers discovered several oxides with lower thermal conductivity than 7YSZ, as described in reports #6-8.
The researchers re-examined the commonly used thermal flash test and developed new, numerically-based data reduction methods for extracting thermal diffusivity.
The researchers described a new method for determining thermal diffusivity of coatings on oxidized bond-coats that takes advantage of the luminescence signal from the underlying oxide scale.
The researchers investigated the thermal cyclic life of current 7YSZ EB-PVD coatings, as described in reports #14-16.
The researchers found that the diffuse reflectance correlates well with the coating density, suggesting the potential for non-contact evaluation of coatings.
Detailed measurements of the optical properties of tetragonal YSZ were made in collaboration with colleagues at the National Institute for Materials Science in Japan.
The researchers investigated a number of non-contact methods for measuring the temperature of 7YSZ thermal barrier coatings.
The researchers found that the existing method of determining thermal conductivity of low conductivity oxides and coatings is fraught with measurement uncertainty.
